name: Ramp
text: Add a persistent skip link at the top of every page that jumps to the main content. This lets keyboard users bypass repetitive headers or nav blocks in one keystroke, fixing a core keyboard-nav failure without changing visual layout. The trade-off is a small extra DOM node and a fixed-position button, but the benefit—immediate access for screen-reader and switch users—outweighs the cost.

name: Reader
text: Adding a persistent skip link may not fully address the navigation issues for all users. It risks creating a separate accessibility issue if the link is not visually identifiable or lacks proper focus styles, which can confuse users relying on keyboard navigation. A better alternative is to ensure a logical heading structure and provide clear keyboard shortcuts for key sections to enhance overall navigability without introducing additional complexities. Testing with real users would help validate which solution provides the best experience.
